h2: ASNT NDT Level III preparation for Portland candidates, and who hires Level IIIs locally
html:
ASNT NDT Level III preparation for Portland candidates, and who hires Level IIIs locally

Candidates in Portland prepare for the ASNT NDT Level III the same way candidates do everywhere. They study online for the Basic examination and at least one method examination, and ASNT handles eligibility, testing and the certificate. Atlantis runs that preparation online. Locally, Level IIIs are hired by ship repair yards, fuel terminal and pipeline operators, and inspection companies working on both sides of the Columbia.

The national route, step by step. The ASNT NDT Level III is a central certification issued by ASNT, not by your employer. It starts with the Basic examination, which covers SNT-TC-1A and the other personnel standards, materials and processes, and general familiarity with other methods. Each method examination, such as UT, RT, MT, PT or VT, adds that method to the certificate. ASNT publishes the education and experience you need before you may sit, and it sets its own examination charges, so check its current rules before you book. Many employer written practices then use the ASNT certificate as the evidence behind the person they name as Level III. Atlantis's ASNT NDT Level III exam preparation follows that route, and the course cost for your country is shown when you register.

Who hires Level IIIs around Portland. Vigor Marine Group, formed in 2025 from Vigor Industrial and its sister companies, is headquartered in Portland. Its original yard is on Swan Island, with three dry docks, including The Vigorous, a 960-foot floating dry dock delivered in 2014. Ship repair at that scale needs someone who owns the procedures, answers the surveyor, and approves subcontracted inspection. Fuel is a second source of jobs. Most of Oregon's petroleum products come from Washington refineries by the Olympic Pipeline and by barge. Portland terminals start the distribution, including Kinder Morgan's roughly 115-mile products line to Eugene. Pipeline and terminal operators working under PHMSA rules need qualified weld and integrity-dig procedures and someone accountable for them.

Two states, one metro. Vigor also runs a smaller facility in Vancouver, Washington, and many Portland technicians work across the river. Washington applies its own rules. Pressure vessels there fall under the Department of Labor & Industries, and industrial radiography needs a Washington Department of Health license or reciprocity. A Level III working both banks keeps the written practice and procedures in step with both states.

  • Basic plus method examinations, taken through ASNT
  • Eligibility set by ASNT's published education and experience routes
  • Ship repair: procedure ownership and subcontractor approval
  • Pipelines and terminals: procedures for welds and integrity digs

Next steps. For employer-side Level III functions rather than an exam, see NDT consulting in Portland and maritime Level III consulting in Portland. Level I and II technicians start with NDT training in Portland, and anyone can practice method skills on the Practical NDT simulator for Portland. Questions about readiness or eligibility can go to the Portland Level III enquiry.
